skill.name: routeros-qemu-chr
skill.description: Run MikroTik RouterOS CHR images with QEMU. Covers x86_64 and aarch64 boot paths, VirtIO devices, acceleration choices, port forwarding, CI patterns, and licensing.
skill.summary: Guides RouterOS CHR boot, testing, and CI workflows in QEMU.
skill.author: tikoci

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, or malicious intent was found. The skill is legitimate RouterOS CHR and QEMU guidance, but it includes privileged host changes, external downloads, VM process launch, local service exposure, and predictable temp paths. These risks should be documented and gated by user confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: KVM permission changes use sudo and set broad device access.
remediation.suggestion: Limit the udev rule to isolated CI runners. Avoid MODE=0666 on shared or self-hosted hosts.

remediation.issue: Examples launch QEMU and download images or packages from remote sources.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before execution. Prefer checksums or pinned RouterOS versions when possible.

remediation.issue: Default empty admin credentials appear in REST and SSH examples.
remediation.suggestion: State that empty credentials are only for fresh local CHR instances. Require passwords for persistent labs.

remediation.issue: QEMU sockets, logs, PIDs, and vars files use predictable /tmp paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use per-instance directories with restrictive permissions and safe cleanup.

remediation.issue: The CI retry pattern includes destructive git cleanup commands.
remediation.suggestion: Warn that these commands belong only in disposable CI worktrees, not developer worktrees.

content.value_statement: RouterOS CHR labs often fail because firmware, VirtIO, acceleration, and port forwarding differ by architecture. This skill provides tested QEMU patterns for local labs and CI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Selects SeaBIOS or UEFI boot paths for CHR images.
Explains VirtIO disk and network choices for x86_64 and aarch64.
Provides QEMU launch patterns for shell, Bun, and CI usage.
Maps localhost port forwards for WebFig, REST, SSH, API, and WinBox.
Documents CHR licensing behavior, trials, and common boot failures.
limitations: Does not configure RouterOS services after the VM boots.
Requires QEMU, CHR images, and valid local permissions.
Some examples need sudo or KVM access on the host.
Hardware acceleration depends on host OS and guest architecture.

use_cases.title: Build a Disposable RouterOS Lab
use_cases.description: Create a local CHR VM for API testing, packet debugging, or training without hardware.

use_cases.title: Add RouterOS Integration Tests
use_cases.description: Run CHR in GitHub Actions to validate REST, packages, and generated schemas.

use_cases.title: Diagnose CHR Boot Problems
use_cases.description: Compare firmware, CPU, acceleration, and VirtIO choices when a VM stalls or times out.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a CHR Lab
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a RouterOS CHR QEMU lab on my host. Ask for my host OS and CPU architecture if needed, then recommend the image, boot method, acceleration, RAM, disk, and port forwards.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Boot Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this CHR boot failure: [symptoms]. Compare firmware, machine type, disk interface, CPU model, and VirtIO transport. Give a prioritized fix list.

prompt_templates.title: Create a CI Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub Actions workflow for a selected RouterOS CHR version. Include image download, disk conversion, QEMU startup, REST readiness checks, optional package upload, reboot handling, and safe cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Arch Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a multi-architecture CHR test strategy for x86_64 and aarch64 hosts. Include acceleration fallback rules, unsupported combinations, boot timing expectations, and skip logic.

output_examples.input: I need an x86_64 CHR lab on Linux with REST access.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a launch plan using SeaBIOS, VirtIO disk and network, KVM when available, and localhost REST forwarding.

output_examples.input: My aarch64 VM boots to a silent stall.
output: A diagnosis that checks UEFI pflash sizing and CPU model first.
A reminder to use explicit VirtIO PCI devices instead of the aarch64 shorthand.
A fallback plan for TCG when hardware acceleration is unavailable.

output_examples.input: I need CI to test RouterOS package behavior.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines image download, disk conversion, QEMU startup, readiness checks, package upload, reboot handling, and cleanup.

best_practices: Bind forwarded services to localhost unless remote access is required.
Use per-instance temp paths for QEMU sockets, logs, and firmware variables.
Confirm CHR license limits before testing throughput or package downloads.
anti_patterns: Do not use aarch64 if=virtio shorthand for RouterOS disks.
Do not assume KVM or HVF works across host and guest architectures.
Do not reuse empty admin passwords outside disposable local CHR instances.

faq.question: Does this skill install RouterOS?
faq.answer: No. It explains how to obtain CHR images and run them with QEMU.

faq.question: Can it run on macOS?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers HVF, Homebrew firmware paths, and CPU model constraints.

faq.question: Why does aarch64 need UEFI?
faq.answer: The arm64 CHR image boots through EDK2 pflash firmware, not SeaBIOS.

faq.question: Is the free CHR license enough for CI?
faq.answer: Yes for API tests. Throughput is limited to 1 Mbps.

faq.question: Does it configure RouterOS after boot?
faq.answer: No. Use a RouterOS configuration skill or CLI workflow after CHR is reachable.

faq.question: Are the CI examples safe on shared runners?
faq.answer: They need review. Some steps use sudo, KVM permissions, local port forwards, and predictable temp paths.
